facts.text: The 1959 magnitude‑7.5 earthquake instantly dammed the Madison River, forming Quake Lake and burying a campground, killing 28 people.
Bleached tree trunks still standing in Hebgen Lake's shallows, decades after the 1959 earthquake dropped this section of shoreline.
Hebgen Lake was created in 1914 by building Hebgen Dam, impounding the Madison River into a reservoir 15 miles long and 4 miles wide.
The lake sits at the base of the Madison, Gallatin, and Centennial ranges, just north of the Montana‑Idaho‑Wyoming border, and many visitors treat it as part of Yellowstone.
Hebgen Lake is consistently rated among the best stillwater fly fishing lakes in North America, drawing anglers who plan entire trips around it.
The lake's open water makes it a favorite for sailing, but wind can build quickly by afternoon.
